why this proves self-containment
---------------------------------
MediaHub.EngineProbe tries NativeLibrary.Load(<absolute path>) first and only falls back to
AddDllDirectory(--deps) + SetDefaultDllDirectories, then to LoadLibraryExW, when that fails.
The report records loadMode=native-library only when the Windows loader resolved every imported
DLL on its own. PATH carried no MSYS2 or prefix entry, so the third-party DLLs in
windows/engine/lgpl/dist could not be borrowed from C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin or
D:\mh-servers\lgpl-build\prefix\bin: they were found next to libmpv-2.dll, which is exactly how
the product loads them (the app copies them into its own output directory).

scope and limits
----------------
GPU, HDR and audio output are not exercised (vo=null, ao=null, hwdec=no) - same caveat as the CI
engine step. The 44 Windows DLLs listed in the manifest header are left to the OS (System32 and the
api-ms-win-* API sets) and must not be shipped. Reproduce with the command line above after
running: pwsh -File windows/tools/collect-lgpl-runtime.ps1
